processing: Orthodox Ceylon black tea in grades such as FBOPF1 and BOPSP.
harvest_season: Little is published on a best season for this estate; as elsewhere in Uva, it is picked through the year with dry-weather lots usually most valued.
appearance_dry: Dark orthodox leaf, its size set by the grade.
appearance_liquor: Clear reddish amber, as with mid-grown Uva teas.
taste_profile: Little is recorded in detail; expect a medium-bodied, rounded Ceylon black tea, typical of mid-elevation Uva.

brewing.notes: Brewed Western style. Shorten the steep for small broken grades.

vintage_note: Sold through the Colombo auction by grade, without a vintage; the record lots were marketed by Forbes and Walker. Drink recent lots within a year or two.
description:
Shawlands is a mid-elevation estate at Lunugala in Uva, at about 990 metres on the southern slopes of the Madulsima range. It is managed by Hapugastenna Plantations, and it is a name the auction room knows better than the tea shelf.

The tea is orthodox black, and small grades such as FBOPF1 and BOPSP have set estate records at auction. The Sri Lanka Tea Board has also given it a two-star rating for its organising and manufacturing practices.

Brew it like other mid-grown Ceylon black tea, with water just off the boil, and shorten the steep for small grades, which stand up well to milk.

Look for Lunugala or Uva on the pack to be sure of the origin.
history: Its recent reputation comes from the Colombo auction, where it has set estate records, including Rs. 1,160 per kilo for an FBOPF1 in August 2021, in the Uva Medium category.
